title: AU Small Finance Bank Raises NRI Deposit Rates Amid India's Record Dollar Drive
excerpt: The bank hiked FCNR rates to 7.10% and introduced zero-cost remittances as part of a broader RBI-backed push that has drawn $32 billion in foreign currency inflows.
body:
• AU Small Finance Bank raised its peak FCNR (B) deposit rate from 5.15% to 7.10% p.a. for US dollar deposits, effective June 10, 2026.
  • Fixed deposit rates were also revised upward to 7.40% for regular customers and 7.90% for senior citizens.
  • The bank introduced zero forex margin and zero bank charges on eligible NRI remittances, eliminating markups that can erode up to 2% of transfer value.
  • The moves come as Indian banks have collectively raised $32 billion under RBI-backed dollar inflow schemes, with the FCNR window open until September 30.

Rate Hike Details

AU Small Finance Bank, India's largest small finance bank, raised its peak Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) deposit rate from 5.15% per annum to 7.10% per annum, effective June 10, 2026, according to the bank's press release. The semi-annually paid interest applies to US dollar-denominated deposits, which are fully repatriable and exempt from Indian income tax on both principal and interest.

The bank simultaneously revised fixed deposit rates to 7.40% from 7.25% for regular customers and to 7.90% from 7.75% for senior citizens. Recurring deposit rates received identical increases.

Zero-Cost Remittance Push

Alongside the rate hikes, AU SFB introduced zero forex margin and zero bank charges on eligible inward and outward remittances. The bank described itself as the only private sector bank in India to eliminate embedded forex markups on these transactions.

Under the new proposition, eligible customers receive currency conversion at the bank's Interbank Reference Rate with no additional transaction charges. Typical forex markups can erode up to 2% of transfer value, according to the bank, making the elimination a meaningful cost saving for NRIs moving money between countries.

RBI's Dollar Inflow Campaign

AU SFB's rate revision sits within a broader Reserve Bank of India campaign to attract foreign currency into the country. On June 5, the RBI announced a concessional swap facility under which it bears the full hedging cost for banks mobilizing fresh 3-to-5-year FCNR deposits. On June 17, the central bank went further, temporarily withdrawing the interest rate ceiling on FCNR deposits of those tenors until September 30, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

The results have been dramatic. Indian banks have raised close to $32 billion under these schemes, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra told The Hindu BusinessLine in an interview published on July 27, with most of the inflows coming through FCNR deposits. The figure already surpasses the $26 billion mobilized during India's landmark 2013 FCNR drive, which took nearly three months.

"We do not find any prima facie evidence of recirculation of the existing deposits, in whatever form, to be of any significance or concern."

— Sanjay Malhotra, RBI Governor

SBI Research estimates that FCNR deposits alone could reach $65–70 billion by the time the window closes in September, with total inflows across all RBI-linked channels projected at $80–85 billion, according to Outlook Business.

What This Means for NRIs

The combination of higher rates and zero-cost remittances creates a materially improved proposition for overseas Indians looking to park dollars in India. FCNR deposits have historically offered modest returns—often trailing US money market rates—but the current rates of 6–7% across major banks represent a sharp departure, driven by the RBI's willingness to absorb hedging costs.

The tax advantage adds to the appeal: FCNR deposits are exempt from Indian income tax on both principal and interest, and since they are denominated in foreign currency, depositors bear no exchange rate risk for the tenure of the deposit.

AU SFB, which received in-principle approval from the RBI to transition into a universal bank—the first such approval in over a decade—serves more than 1.2 crore customers through 2,790 banking touchpoints across 21 states and 4 union territories. NRI customers can access the revised rates through the bank's digital channels, including its AU 0101 app, WhatsApp Banking, and 24/7 video banking.

What's Next

The FCNR window remains open until September 30, 2026, while ECB and overseas foreign currency borrowing channels run until December 31. Most FCNR deposits maturing in August and September are expected to renew under the new facility, according to SBI Research, further boosting inflows. With multiple banks competing aggressively for NRI deposits, rates could remain elevated through the scheme's duration.
nri_angle: NRIs can now earn up to 7.10% on dollar deposits with zero forex charges on remittances, a sharp improvement from rates below 5.15% just weeks earlier.
